(i) successful literature can be predicted by stylometry with accuracy as high as 84%, (ii) successful novels are more likely to have more complex sentence structures and more sophisticated vocabulary, and (iii) successful novels are less readable.

statistical stylometry is a promising tool to predict the success of literature, and that successful novels have a more distinctive writing style, with a higher proportion of unique words, a more diverse word usage, a higher average word length, and a lower readability.

(1) statistical stylometry can effectively discriminate successful literary works, (2) successful literary works tend to have higher lexical diversity than unsuccessful works, and (3) successful literary works are more likely to have higher readability and lower word frequency than less successful works, which are counterintuitive to conventional wisdom.
